name: Excel Exercises
description: Hands-on drills for Excel functions and keyboard shortcuts. A few lessons are free, then a hard paywall. Solo founder Jake, a finance graduate who taught himself to code. He built it at night, five or six years ago.

mentions.evidence: Self-reported, shown in a Starter Story interview on 28 October 2026. Not independently checked. $30,000 to $35,000 a month. A little over $30,000 in the past four weeks. About 2,500 paying subscribers. About 50,000 visitors in the past four weeks. He says it grew about five times since he quit his job two years ago, and that doubling the monthly price, while leaving the annual price alone, is what made growth take off.
mentions.indieAngle: Drills for one office tool, a hard paywall, search first, then a boss buying seats.

whyItPrints: New graduates, and people who overstated Excel on a CV, need to get competent fast. He says growth came from long search pages, then ads, then bosses buying fifty seats and universities buying a class. He says the hosting bill is under $100 a month.
whyThisMatters:
Excel Exercises is drills for functions and shortcuts. A few lessons are free. Then the paywall. Jake built it alone, at night, five or six years ago. He studied finance and taught himself to code.

He says the monthly take is in a band around thirty thousand, with a little over that in the past four weeks, about twenty-five hundred paying people, and about fifty thousand visitors. He says it grew several times over after he quit his job, and that raising the monthly price, while leaving the yearly price alone, is what unlocked it. Hosting, he says, is tiny. The path was search pages, then ads, then a boss buying a block of seats or a university buying a class. All of that is from a Starter Story interview on 28 October 2026. I did not check the payment account.

You pay so the spreadsheet skill is real before someone asks you to use it.
